newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Southern Life's investment arm aims high.
newsitem.headline: Southern Life's investment arm aims high.

text.p: Southern Asset Management (SAM), a unit of South African insurance firm Southern Life Association Ltd, said on Wednesday it was restructuring with the aim of becoming the country's leading investment manager by the turn of the century.

SAM's chief executive officer Neil Cochrane said the move, which included the appointement of 10 investment professionals, aimed to address the uncompetitive investment performance that continued to spook Southern Life's pension fund business.
"We have set ourselves the goal of being the market's preferred investment manager by the year 2000," Cochrane told a news conference.

He said SAM, which manages investment assets worth about 35 billion rand, wanted to shift from the country's traditional investment approach which did not ensure co-ordinated investment decisions between portfolio managers of the same firm.

"Inefficiencies in the South African market can be turned to opportunities. Through careful research and development we have devised a focused team-based approach...designed to offer flexibility, consistently good investment returns and reduced investment risk," Cochrane said.
SAM would restructure its core portfolios to produce stable performances in line with industry averages while complementing these with specialist satellite portfolios designed to outperform.

Cochrane, appointed last October to spearhead SAM's transformation, said the unit would investigate potential joint ventures and acquisitions to enhance its long term stature among its clients and products.
"Joint ventures and everything like that will be very nice for us. We will try to look at these in the future," he told Reuters.
